card.title: KM TIRPITZ
card.text: Deal 4 damage to the enemy HQ. The enemy cannot deploy units next turn.
card.flavorText: The Tirpitz was the second of two Bismarck-class battleships built for Germany's Kriegsmarine during WWII. It was named after Grand Admiral Alfred von Tirpitz. The ship was commissioned in February 1941 and at the time she was the heaviest battleship ever built for a European Navy, weighing over 52,000 tons at full load. In 1941 Tirpitz briefly served in the Baltic Fleet to prevent a possible breakout by the Soviet Baltic Fleet. In early 1942, she was deployed to Norway to deter an Allied invasion and to intercept Arctic convoys supplying the Soviet Union. Although she attempted to engage Allied convoys, during Operation Rösselsprung in July 1942 for instance, these missions were largely unsuccessful. Nevertheless, her presence tied down significant British naval resources. Tirpitz's only offensive action occurred in September 1943, when she, alongside the battleship Scharnhorst, bombarded Allied positions on the island of Spitzbergen. Soon after, she suffered damage from a British midget submarine attack and was subjected to multiple air raids. On 12 November 1944, British Lancaster bombers equipped with 12,000-pound "Tallboy" bombs struck Tirpitz, causing her to capsize rapidly. The attack resulted in the deaths of between 950 and 1,204 crew members. Between 1948 and 1957, the wreck was salvaged by a joint Norwegian and German operation.
